patch.value: GH-1676: a pm close refused for missing close fields suggests a separate pm update and a retry, although pm close accepts --resolution, --expected-result and --actual-result itself

GitHub issue #1676 (reported 2026-11-06 against 2026.11.5). Reproduced 2026-11-06 on main af6fd5583 (2026.11.6) in a disposable non-git tracker: pm --no-extensions --pm-path .agents/pm close lab-one done --validate-close strict exits 2 with close_validation_missing_fields. The recovery bundle's suggested_retry is pm --pm-path .agents/pm --no-extensions update lab-one --resolution "<value>" --expected-result "<value>" --actual-result "<value>", and next_steps say "Run the suggested pm update, then retry the original pm close invocation." pm close declares --resolution, --expected-result (alias --expected) and --actual-result (alias --actual) itself, so the single close call succeeds. Following the advertised route costs two writes, two history entries and two lock cycles, leaves a window where the item carries close evidence while still open, and moves updated_at (which reorders downstream changelog sections, unbraind/pm-changelog#323). GH-757 fixed the same class for pm update --status closed. Cause: collectCloseValidationWarnings in src/sdk/lifecycle/close.ts renders an update command from commandScope, and the CLI recovery builder keeps a producer suggested_retry verbatim. Expected: suggested_retry and suggested_retry_args are the caller's own close invocation with each missing flag appended before any -- terminator (every other token, including tracker scope, --json and --expect-hash, preserved; an empty supplied value is replaced rather than duplicated), next_steps name that single command, and the update route stays as a secondary next_best_command. SDK callers without argv get a close command rendered from the item id, reason and command scope. Duplicate check: searched suggested_retry close refusal; pm-p316vn (GH-953, closed) preserved supplied flags for the close_reason path, pm-ulqu (GH-519, closed) fixed the enum placeholder, pm-5uclvd (GH-885, closed) fixed create-time close_reason_required. None covers the missing close-field refusal recommending a different command.

A strict close refused for missing close fields returns suggested_retry and suggested_retry_args equal to the caller's own pm close invocation with each missing flag appended before any -- terminator, preserving tracker scope, --json and every other supplied token; An empty supplied close field (for example --resolution with an empty string, or its --expected/--actual alias) is replaced in the retry rather than duplicated; next_steps name the single pm close retry first and keep the pm update route only as a secondary next_best_command; SDK callers without an invocation argv receive a pm close command rendered from the item id, reason and command scope; A spec executes the emitted suggested_retry_args against a sandbox tracker and the item closes in one write with one history entry
A strict close refused for missing close fields suggests the same pm close with the missing flags appended, so one write closes the item

value.text: Implementation evidence (branch fix/recovery-replays-invocation). Producer: closeValidationMissingFieldsError in src/sdk/lifecycle/close.ts now renders suggested_retry as a pm close (scope, id, reason, missing flags), keeps the pm update route as recovery.next_best_command, names the flags in required, and next_steps say to retry the same close. CLI: new src/cli/runtime/close-fields-retry.ts (repairCloseFieldsRecovery, wired into repairInvocationRecovery in src/cli/main.ts) rebuilds the retry from the caller's exact argv with each missing flag inserted before any -- terminator. It walks the global plus command flag contracts so declared option values are consumed (a flag-looking --reason value is kept), and removes blank supplied values under every alias (--expected=, --actual " "). If the command does not declare every missing flag, or an option's arity is unknown, the producer recovery is kept. Verified: the sandbox replay of the emitted suggested_retry_args closes in one write (history create plus close only). tests/integration/recovery-replays-invocation.integration.spec.ts executes it end to end, tests/unit/cli/runtime/close-fields-retry.spec.ts covers the repair edges, close-command.spec.ts asserts the SDK producer shape. Negative control: disabling the repair fails the integration spec.

patch.value: suggested_retry is the same pm close plus the missing flags, preserving tracker scope, --json and --expect-hash. Replaying it closes the item in one write with one history entry.

The producer in src/sdk/lifecycle/close.ts renders the retry as a pm close and keeps the pm update route as recovery.next_best_command. The new CLI repair src/cli/runtime/close-fields-retry.ts rebuilds suggested_retry and suggested_retry_args from the caller's exact argv with each missing flag inserted before any -- terminator. It is contract-aware: declared option values are consumed, and blank values under any alias are replaced. When the command cannot accept a field itself, or an option's arity is unknown, it keeps the producer's recovery.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) on PR #1680 head b0a334fa1: 6 findings on this item, all verified and fixed.
(P1) Short options -m/-r/-d were unknown to the contract-based scan, so the repair fell back to the producer retry and dropped --expect-hash. The scan now uses the parser's own Commander option table (global plus command options, passed from main.ts invokedCommandOptions): long and short spellings, attached short values (-rText) and boolean clusters (-qa).
(P2) --validate-close [mode] consumed the next token even when that token is option-shaped. Optional values are now consumed only when Commander would consume them.
(P2) argv.indexOf("--") matched a -- consumed as a required value (--pm-path --, --reason --). The terminator is now found during the option-aware scan.
(P2) When arity cannot be proven, the retry is withdrawn instead of replaced by one that drops the caller's tokens. missing and next_best_command stay.
(P2) The SDK retry dropped supplied options. It now carries resolution, expected/actual result, validate-close, completed-at, message, author and force as attached --flag=value tokens.
(P2) A hyphen-leading SDK reason became a flag. The reason is now rendered as --reason=<text>.
The integration spec now replays -m plus --expect-hash. After a peer edit the replayed retry refuses with exit 4 (the guard survived), and with a fresh hash it closes in one write.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Review round 3 on PR #1680 head 6107aeac8 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh, 4 findings, all verified and fixed). Rounds 1 to 3 showed that re-implementing Commander's two parse passes (global options first, then command options) in a token scan cannot be made exact. The repair no longer parses or removes anything.
- It appends the missing flags after every typed token. Each is a complete option at a boundary of a parse that succeeded, and the parser keeps the last value of a repeated option, so the appended flag also overrides a blank supplied value. Verified live: close --resolution "" ... --resolution r records r.
- When a -- follows the command, the flags go directly after the command token. If the caller typed any spelling of a missing field after the command, the retry is withdrawn.
- (P1) When the invocation named no tracker, the environment-selected tracker from resolvePmCommandScopeArgs is prepended, so a PM_PATH selection is kept.
- (P2) A typed producer missing list now suppresses the CLI's message-text inference (inferMissingFieldsForRecovery in src/cli/main.ts). A withdrawn retry, for example from close-task, which cannot accept the evidence flags, is no longer rebuilt as close-task --validate-close "<value>".
Specs: close-fields-retry.spec.ts covers these rules (environment tracker included), and the integration spec adds a close-task envelope case run in-process.

value.text:
Review round 4 on PR #1680 head 002f4bb0a (Codex, 3 findings; CodeRabbit full review, 3 findings), all verified.
- Tracker detection no longer scans tokens, which misread a literal --pm-path=... reason after --. main.ts passes the environment scope (resolvePmCommandScopeArgs) as a prefix only when the parsed bootstrap globals carry no tracker path.
- The SDK retry asks for --reason=<reason> when an SDK-only lifecycle override (lifecyclePolicy.requireCloseReason false) waived a reason the CLI would demand.
- runAction drops only the trailing --no-extensions that resolvePmCommandScopeArgs appended, never a tracker value spelled the same.
- Message-text inference is now skipped only for close_validation_missing_fields. Other typed-missing refusals, such as assurance --owner, keep inference.
- Added duplicate-check comments, with related edges, on pm-gh1678, pm-gh1679 and pm-t5gari.
Full suite 12118 passed, coverage 100/100/100/100.

value.text: Review round 5 on PR #1680 head 204f88d61 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh, 1 finding, verified and fixed). An SDK closeItem with a lifecyclePolicy override (requireCloseReason or orderingEdges) has no CLI spelling, so a suggested CLI close would perform a different transition: orderingEdges remove would become the default preserve. Such a refusal now carries no CLI retry. Its required and next_steps tell the caller to retry the same SDK close with the evidence supplied, and recovery keeps missing plus the replayable pm update route. This supersedes the round-4 --reason=<reason> placeholder. The spec covers both override keys.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Review round 6 on PR #1680 head 38d051b21 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh, 2 findings, verified and fixed).
(1) An SDK or MCP close guarded by expectHash got a CLI retry without the guard, because the runtime strips expectHash before dispatch and only CLI argv is repaired. A new core helper, activeItemRevisionExpectations, reads the active scope's expectation for the item, and the producer renders it as --expect-hash=<id>=<hash>.
(2) A typed empty tracker option (--pm-path "" or --pm-path=) is read by the bootstrap parse as no selection, but the parser keeps it as the option's last value, so a prepended environment tracker would not bind. main.ts marks empty values and asks the real bootstrap scanner whether one of them is a tracker value (typedEmptyTrackerOption). When an environment scope would be needed, it passes null and the repair withdraws the retry.
Specs: a runAction close with expectHash, and in-process CLI cases from inside another workspace with PM_PATH set: no empty option gives the env-scoped retry; --pm-path "" and --pm-path= give no retry. Full suite 12120 passed, coverage 100/100/100/100.

value.text: Codex review round 9 (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) on 1e9251443 found two embedded-CLI compositions that dropped SDK revision guards from the close retry. (1) Nested same-tracker SDK scopes binding different hashes for a dependent: the producer withdrew its retry, but repairCloseFieldsRecovery rebuilt one from argv because missing was set, with no guard. It now returns the producer's recovery unchanged when the producer proposed no retry. (2) typedGuard matched any argv token ending in =<hash>, so --message=<hash> suppressed the producer's --expect-hash=<dep>=<hash>. The repair now appends every --expect-hash=<id>=<hash> token from the producer retry and matches nothing against argv: a guard the caller also typed repeats at the same revision, which bindItemRevisionScope accepts. Executed in a sandbox: pm close <id> Done --expect-hash <h> --message=<h> --validate-close strict refuses with exit 2, and its suggested_retry_args, with placeholders filled, closes the item (exit 0) despite the repeated guard. Specs: close-fields-retry.spec.ts (hash-valued message/reason, producer-withdrawn retry) and item-revision.spec.ts (embedded runCliInProcess inside conflicting nested scopes and with a hash-valued message). Negative control: restoring the 1e9251443 repair fails three close-fields-retry cases.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 10 (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) on 3d878121e found three follow-ups to appending every producer guard. (1) The filter read the producer scope too, so a tracker named --expect-hash=bad (pm --pm-path=--expect-hash=bad close ...) became a guard and the replay failed with expect_hash_invalid; producerRevisionGuards now reads only the run of --expect-hash=<id>=<hash> tokens the producer places directly before its trailing placeholders. (2) A write inside the refused operation (a beforeCommand hook, or an SDK update inside the same scope) advances a guard past its declared revision, so the caller's typed guard and the producer's advanced one conflict (expected_revision_duplicate); activeItemRevisionExpectations now reports such a scope as unreplayable and the producer withdraws the CLI retry with SDK-only guidance. (3) recovery-replays-invocation.integration.spec.ts now expects the repeated producer guard and refreshes every spelling of the decided hash before the successful replay. Executed: on a tracker literally named --expect-hash=bad, the strict close's filled retry closes the item (exit 0). Negative controls: restoring the unrestricted filter fails the tracker-operand case, and dropping the advanced-revision check fails the in-scope update case in item-revision.spec.ts.

value.text: Codex review round 11 (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) on abdeec1b2 confirmed the round 9-10 fixes with read-only probes and found one tracker-scope gap: with an environment-selected tracker, pm --pm-path=' ' close ... resolves the environment tracker (resolvePmRoot trims the value), but closeRetryScopePrefix treated the whitespace value as an explicit tracker and prepended no scope, so the replayed retry could select the cwd tracker. A final tracker value that trims to empty is now blank like an empty one (the empty mark became a space, so one trim check covers both), and the retry is withdrawn when an environment scope would be needed. The integration spec adds --pm-path ' ' and --pm-path='  '; restoring the previous check fails it.
